acceptance: The record names where subagents are launched and whether the limit can be enforced there; if the launcher is outside this repository, the owner is told exactly what to change.
The proposed limit is justified from the ledger: queue depth and watchdog kills against agent count over 13 to 15 November.
No agent-facing instruction text is added.
context: Found during a retrospective on 2026-11-15. The guard-side fixes are in PR BenchBox-dev/benchbox#4236. Guardrails: linked worktree, one PR; no live-cloud runs; heavy work only via lock-taking entry points; re-verify cited facts before acting.
description:
Problem: on 13 and 14 November, three and then nine subagents ran on a 16 GiB, 10-CPU host with swap near 95 percent. The heavy-work ledger shows four watchdog kills in eight minutes, and at times more than six heavy-run commands queued. Agents treated 'Error 79' and refusals as noise to retry past. Throughput was lost to queueing and to results taken under load.

Outcome: a decision on a concurrency limit derived from host capacity (memory and CPUs, for example the admission check's own readings), applied where agents are dispatched, and a record of where that dispatch code lives. This is not an instruction to agents.
drop_reason: Owner decision 2026-11-16: no concurrency cap; rely on the existing admission check, which now also refuses on load (PR 4236, 4251).
